item.title: Simultaneous popular polynomial differences in higher dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.30335v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the simultaneous popular polynomial difference theorem of Conlon, Dong, and the author to polynomial shifts along prescribed directions in $\mathbb{F}_p^D$. Let $P_1,\ldots,P_k\in\mathbb{Z}[t]$ be linearly independent polynomials with zero constant terms, and let $v_1,\ldots,v_k\in\mathbb{Z}^D\setminus\{0\}$. We show that, for every $\varepsilon>0$, every sufficiently large prime $p$, and every $A\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p^D$ of density $\alpha$, there exists a nonzero $d\in\mathbb{F}_p$ such that \[ \mathbb{E}_{\underline{x}\in\mathbb{F}_p^D} \mathbf{1}_A(\underline{x}) \prod_{\substack{1\leq i\leq k\\ \omega_i=1}} \mathbf{1}_A\bigl(\underline{x}+P_i(d)v_i\bigr) \geq \alpha^{\,1+\sum_{i=1}^k\omega_i}-\varepsilon \] simultaneously for every $\omega\in\{0,1\}^k$. The main new ingredient is a directional arithmetic regularity decomposition adapted to mixed directional box norms.
item.dc:creator: Guo-Dong Hong

item.title: An explicit elementary proof of no Landau--Siegel zeros
item.description: arXiv:2610.30476v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give an elementary proof of the absence of Landau--Siegel zeros with the explicit constant $c=1/100$. For every primitive quadratic Dirichlet character $\chi$ of conductor $q\ge3$, each real zero $\beta\in(0,1)$ of $L(s,\chi)$ satisfies $(1-\beta)\log q>c$. The proof combines integer coefficient counting, polynomial congruences, a paired-tail hyperbola estimate, and a logarithmically weighted comparison of positive sums. All required constants are explicit, and one choice of parameters covers every conductor. The argument uses elementary arithmetic and real summation and integration, without separate zero computations for small conductors.
item.dc:creator: Victor Zhenyu Guo

item.title: Norm-Euclideanity in cyclic fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.30621v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Consider a cyclic number field of prime degree $p$. For a fixed degree, there are only finitely many such fields which are norm-Euclidean. When $p=2$ or $3$, these have been completely determined. If instead $p>3$, one can bound the discriminant of such fields from above. We substantially sharpen these upper bounds via an explicit Burgess-type criterion and describe a method for completely resolving other small prime cases.
item.dc:creator: Gustav Kj{\ae}rbye Bagger

item.title: On the Open Problem in the 2023 Simon Marais Mathematics Competition
item.description: arXiv:2610.30658v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that, for $n \in \mathbb{Z}^+$ not a perfect square, the only pairs of positive integers $\{a, b\}$ for which there exists $r \in \mathbb{R}$ such that $r^a + \sqrt{n}$ and $r^b + \sqrt{n}$ are both rational numbers are those of the form $\{a, a\}$ or $\{g, 2g\}$ (with $g$ odd). This resolves an open question presented in the 2023 Simon Marais Mathematics Competition.
item.dc:creator: Anthony Pisani

item.title: Aspects of quadratic Chabauty via modular forms
item.description: arXiv:2610.30703v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop algorithms to construct a basis of de Rham cohomology for modular curves and a matrix representing the Hodge filtration required in the quadratic Chabauty method. We do this without requiring an explicit plane model of the curve and instead compute these objects in terms of modular forms. Our approach works for any modular curve; to demonstrate its efficiency, we implement our method for nonsplit Cartan modular curves.
item.dc:creator: Marius Leonhardt, Isabel Rendell

item.title: Complete Determination of the Gallai--van der Waerden Number \(\mathrm{GW}(r;3,3)\)
item.description: arXiv:2610.30711v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper completely determines the Gallai--van der Waerden number \(\mathrm{GW}(r;3,3)\) for all integers \(r\ge 3\): \[ \mathrm{GW}(3;3,3)=\mathrm{GW}(4;3,3)=9,\qquad \mathrm{GW}(r;3,3)=r\quad (r\ge 5). \]
item.dc:creator: Yuan Si

item.title: OpenAI partially disproves Littlewood's 1961 $L^\alpha$-flat theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.30797v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a counterexample, produced by OpenAI, to Littlewood's 1961 theorem on $L^\alpha$-flat polynomials. The theorem asserts that no $L^\alpha$-flat polynomials exist within the class of trigonometric polynomials of the form$$\sum_{m=1}^{n} a_m \cos(m\theta+\alpha_m), \qquad n \in \mathbb{N}^*,$$satisfying$$k\, n^2 \sum_{m=1}^{n} a_m^2 \;\leq\; \sum_{m=1}^{n} m^2 a_m^2,$$where $k$ is an absolute constant (alternatively expressed on the right-hand side as $K = 1/k$). We show that OpenAI's counterexample is contained within the class of hyper-lacunary sequences. Consequently, it offers only a limited refutation, as such sequences fail to satisfy an implicit assumption of Littlewood's theorem. We also discuss broader questions surrounding this counterexample and provide a brief historical overview.
item.dc:creator: el Houcein el Abdalaoui

item.title: The exponent $1/4$ in three complexity bounds: integer bases, continued fractions, and the $(3/2)^n$ steering word
item.description: arXiv:2610.30937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\xi$ be a real algebraic irrational number and $p(n,\xi,b)$ the number of distinct blocks of length $n$ in its base-$b$ expansion. Bugeaud and Evertse proved in 2008 that $p(n,\xi,b)/(n(\log n)^\eta)$ is unbounded for every $\eta<1/11$. We prove this for every $\eta<1/4$. We also prove the analogous bound for the continued fraction expansion of an algebraic number of degree at least three, with every exponent $\delta<1/4$. Bugeaud announced this statement in 2013 with an unspecified $\delta>0$. Finally, the subword complexity of the steering word of $(3/2)^n$ exceeds $C\,k(\log k)^\eta$ infinitely often for every $\eta<1/4$ and every $C$. The three proofs share one count: $\varepsilon^{-1}$ classes times $\varepsilon^{-3}$ subspaces from the quantitative Subspace Theorem of Evertse and Ferretti. The subspaces are then disposed of at the cost of a logarithm, with no further power of $\varepsilon^{-1}$. All three results, and the quantitative Subspace Theorem they rest on, are machine-verified in Lean~4.
item.dc:creator: Ralf Stephan

item.title: Irrationality Exponents of Real CM Elliptic Periods and Powers of the Lemniscate Period
item.description: arXiv:2610.31112v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a determinant proof that every nonzero real period of a nonsingular elliptic curve over $\mathbb Q$ with complex multiplication, measured with a specified nonzero rational invariant differential, has irrationality exponent two. The proof uses an integral origin chart, matched local lengths, an actual compactification and weighted packet map, and arithmetic and analytic estimates for the same selected minor on a rectangular sublattice of the full CM period lattice. For the integral-defined lemniscate period $\Omega=2\int_0^1(1-t^4)^{-1/2}\,dt$, we also give the uniform bound $\mu(\Omega^n)=O(n\log(2n))$ for integers $n\geq1$. Its new arithmetic ingredient clears integration denominators prime by prime while retaining the coefficient order; a one-root norm argument and an analytic estimate at algebraic centers complete the power proof. The two arguments are presented with their different charts and exact dependencies. Lean verifies the new CM determinant argument and rational normalization relative to explicit classical uniformization, CM-lifting and theta inputs; the lemniscate-power endpoint is also verified. The formalization record states the exact classical boundary and theorem references.
item.dc:creator: Gregory V. Chudnovsky, David V. Chudnovsky

item.title: On the arithmetic Siegel--Weil formula for orthogonal Shimura varieties over a general totally real field
item.description: arXiv:2610.31173v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathrm{F}/\mathbb{Q}_p$ be a finite extension with $p\ne 2$, and let $V$ be a quadratic space over $\mathrm{F}$ of dimension at least two admitting a self-dual lattice. We prove the local arithmetic Siegel-Weil formula for GSpin Rapoport-Zink spaces formulated by Li and Zhang. We use the global-to-local strategy of Mihatsch and Zhang and its application by Luo. Using a generalization of the prismatic realization functor of Imai, Kato, and Youcis, we construct and study derived special cycles on integral models of SO Shimura varieties and their Rapoport-Zink uniformizations. We derive the local intersection formula from the modularity of special cycles on the generic fiber. As a first application, we prove the corresponding semi-global arithmetic Siegel-Weil identity for orthogonal Shimura varieties over a totally real field $F\ne\mathbb{Q}$.
item.dc:creator: Xuanyou Li

item.title: Landau-Siegel zeros over a base field and effective Brauer-Siegel
item.description: arXiv:2610.31402v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let k be a number field. We prove that for every quadratic extension F/k, every real zero beta of L(s, chi_{F/k}) satisfies (1 - beta) log d_F >= c(k) with an effective constant c(k) > 0, and we deduce (through a reduction of Stark) that the Brauer-Siegel theorem holds effectively and uniformly over all Galois extensions K of k, in the form h_K R_K >= c(k) d_K^{1/2} / ((2 pi)^{[K:Q]} log d_K). Stark's effective cases of the Brauer-Siegel theorem were the fields without quadratic subfields, since the quadratic subfields carried the ineffectivity of Siegel's theorem; over a base field k, the first result removes it. Both rely on a uniform bound for Chebotarev sums. Let K/k be a Galois extension with group G, and suppose S is a subset of G containing the identity. For any prime p of k, let delta_p be the proportion of the primes of K above p whose Frobenius lies in S. Then the sum over Np <= X of delta_p log Np / Np is at most (|S|/|G| + epsilon) log X + O(1), uniformly in K, as soon as X >= d_K^C with C depending only on epsilon and the degree [K:Q]. The proof is Kerr's form of the OpenAI argument, simple vanishing at the points (iota theta)_{iota in S}, with theta in a box in O_K, and Masser's zero estimate. The field enters only through Masser's invariant of the lattice of points, which we compute to be [K:Q]/|S| by averaging over the Galois group of the normal closure. Over Q, the determinant method of Green, Barreto, and Kominers gives sharper Chebotarev bounds, and we explain the comparison.
item.dc:creator: William D. Banks

item.title: Nonvanishing of 2-primary Kolyvagin classes via simultaneous quadratic twists
item.description: arXiv:2610.31631v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $E/\mathbf{Q}$ be an elliptic curve, let $K=\mathbf{Q}(\sqrt{D})$ satisfy the Heegner hypothesis with $D<-4$, and fix a modular parametrization $\varphi$ with $\varphi(\infty)=O$. Under surjectivity modulo $2^L$, with $L\ge 2$, and a cohomological exclusion condition at level $4$, we construct a finite set of primes $T$ such that, writing $d_T=\prod_{q\in T}(-q)$ and $n_T=\prod_{q\in T}q$, the $2$-Selmer dimensions of $E^{d_T}$ and $E^{d_TD}$ are $0$ and $1$. The support size is bounded in terms of the initial Selmer dimensions, independently of $L$. Inspired by the work of Tian and Tian--Yuan--Zhang on congruent numbers, we construct a point $Q_T$ on the terminal twist and identify its Kummer class with the standard mod-$2$ Kolyvagin class. Using the low-corank $2$-converse and the $2$-primary Birch--Swinnerton-Dyer formula, we prove that its index $m_T$ in the full Mordell--Weil lattice satisfies $v_2(m_T)=v_2(c_\varphi)+\mathfrak{i}(E,K)$. The optimal Manin constant theorem supplies a $2$-indivisible parametrization $\varphi_0$, for which $\kappa^{\mathrm{std}}_{n_T,1}(\varphi_0)\ne 0$ if and only if $\mathfrak{i}(E,K)=0$. When the intrinsic index vanishes, the minimum terminal support size is $R=\min\{d_2(E),d_2(E^D)\}$, and the normalized standard classes have order $2^M$ for $1\le M\le L$. Full $2$-adic Galois image then gives strong nonvanishing.
item.dc:creator: Zhiqi Sun

item.title: Denominators of Hodge integrals and Minkowski numbers
item.description: arXiv:2610.30274v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the least common denominator of all genus $g$ Hodge integrals is the Minkowski number $T_{2g}$ or, equivalently, the Bhargava factorial $(2g+1)!_{\mathbb{P}}$ associated to the set of primes $\mathbb{P}\subset\mathbb{N}$. As a corollary, we prove a conjecture of Liu-Xu on the multiplicity of $3$ in the least common denominators of certain descendant integrals, and generalise their result on a conjecture of Itzykson-Zuber to Hodge integrals with $\lambda$ classes. Namely, the order of the automorphism group of any pointed stable curve of genus $g'\le g$ divides the least common denominator of all genus $g$ Hodge integrals. We also comment on the use of generative AI via IMProofBench, which played a fruitful part in the development of this (entirely human-written) paper.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Holmes

item.title: Relative Hitchin fibrations and endoscopy for Unitary Friedberg--Jacquet varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.30366v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a relative fundamental lemma for the unitary symmetric variety $GL_n(k')\backslash U_{2n}$, proving a conjecture of Leslie, Xiao, and Zhang. Our proof reduces to the Lie algebra and argues over function fields in positive characteristic, using methods from Ngo-Laumon and Ngo. In particular, we reinterpret orbital integrals in terms of the cohomology of relative affine Springer fibers and globalize this using unitary versions of Hitchin moduli spaces for symmetric pairs via a product formula. As the main global input, we prove a matching of perverse sheaves between relative Hitchin moduli spaces and their corresponding endoscopic variants.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Hameister, Spencer Leslie

item.title: $\SL_3$ dual pairs
item.description: arXiv:2610.30479v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the exceptional theta correspondence for dual pairs of the form $\SL_3\times G$ inside $p$-adic groups of type $E_n$, $n=6,7,8$. We establish Howe duality for lifts of all Whittaker-generic unitarizable representations of $\SL_3$. Our dual pair is in a see-saw relationship with a dual pair of the form $G_2 \times H$ such that $G/H$ is a rank-two symmetric space. Using the theta correspondence for $\SL_3 \times G$, we prove a multiplicity-one result for $H$-invariant functionals on representations of $G$.
item.dc:creator: Petar Baki\'c, Wee Teck Gan, Gordan Savin

item.title: Asymptotics of local height pairing without Hodge conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.30574v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We remove the assumption of the Hodge conjecture from the asymptotic formula for the Archimedean local height established in our previous work. We also remove other minor assumptions. We achieve this by exploiting the cohomological nature of Beilinson's local intersection index rather than arguing motivically.
item.dc:creator: Yuta Nakayama

item.title: A general quantified Wiener-Ikehara theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.31016v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Building on the technology developed in \cite{Deb-qik}, we establish a quantified Tauberian theorem under a flexible Wiener-Ikehara Tauberian condition and under several types of boundary behavior for the Laplace transform.
item.dc:creator: Gregory Debruyne

item.title: Exact Archimedean Flicker--Rallis Periods on Cohomological Minimal $K$-Types
item.description: arXiv:2610.31018v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For the symmetric pair $(\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb C),\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb R))$, we compute the exact Flicker--Rallis period of a distinguished vector in a cohomological minimal $U(n)$-type, normalized by the Gel'fand--Tsetlin pairing of Hara--Miyazaki--Namikawa. Our main tool is a weight-independent identity between the Whittaker period and a compact $O(n)$-average. We determine the proportionality constant using the archimedean newform formula of Humphries--Jo, and evaluate the compact functional on the normalized distinguished vector. This yields an explicit formula for the Flicker--Rallis period for every cohomological weight.
item.dc:creator: Zheng Wang

item.title: Nonexistence of Constant Congruences for the Cumulative Partition Function
item.description: arXiv:2610.31102v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $p(n)$ be the ordinary partition function and let $c(n)=\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}p(k)$, with $c(0)=0$. We prove that, for every $a\geq1$, $b\geq0$, and $m\geq2$, the sequence $c(an+b)$ is not eventually constant modulo $m$, thereby answering a question posed by Chen. The proof combines the algebraicity over $\mathbb C(j)$ of modular functions for finite-index subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)$ with Voloch's theorem on the transcendence of elliptic modular functions in positive characteristic.
item.dc:creator: Kathy Q. Ji

item.title: Open dynamics with a moving hole: inhomogeneous IFS and exponential separation condition
item.description: arXiv:2610.31128v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal F=\{f_i(x)=r_i x+t_i\}_{i=0}^{b-1}$ be a self-similar iterated function system (IFS) on $\mathbb R$ with $b\ge 3$, and let $K_{\mathcal F}$ be the associated self-similar set. Given $m\in\mathbb N$, for any sequence $\omega=\omega^0\omega^1\ldots$ with each $\omega^i\in \{0,1,\ldots,b-1\}^m$ a block of length $m$, let \[ K_{\mathcal F}^\omega:=\pi_{\mathcal F}\left(\{(d_i)\in \{0,1,\ldots,b-1\}^{\mathbb N}: d_{k+1}d_{k+2}\ldots d_{k+m}\ne\omega^k\quad\forall k\ge 0\}\right), \] where $\pi_{\mathcal F}$ is the natural coding map from $\{0,1,\ldots,b-1\}^{\mathbb N}$ to $K_{\mathcal F}$. The set $K_{\mathcal F}^\omega$ is called the survivor set of an open dynamical system with a moving hole related to $\omega$. When $\mathcal F$ is a homogeneous IFS satisfying the open set condition (OSC), the dimensions of $K_{\mathcal F}^\omega$ were determined by the first author, Sun and Wang (Adv. Math., 2026). In this paper we generalize these results to inhomogeneous IFSs. When $\mathcal F$ satisfies the OSC, we give explicit formulae for the dimensions of $K_{\mathcal F}^\omega$. In particular, we show that the packing dimension and upper box-counting dimension of $K_{\mathcal F}^\omega$ always coincide, while the Hausdorff dimension and lower box-counting dimension of $K_{\mathcal F}^{\omega}$ are not necessarily equal, which is different from the homogeneous case. Furthermore, when $\mathcal F$ satisfies the exponential separation condition and the similarity dimension $s_{\mathcal F}\le 1$, we are able to determine the Hausdorff dimension of $K_{\mathcal F}^\omega$. Finally, we apply our results to badly approximable numbers and non-recurrence points in the setting of inhomogeneous IFS satisfying the OSC.
item.dc:creator: Derong Kong, Kun Li, Cai-Yun Ma, K\'{a}roly Simon

item.title: Log blow-ups and global resolutions in rigid geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.31265v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this article, we study log blow-ups in the setting of log adic spaces. As in the theory of log schemes, we prove the existence of global resolutions of toric singularities for fs log adic spaces log smooth over a $p$-adic field, and the acyclicity of certain sheaves under log blow-ups. One new feature of (log) rigid analytic varieties is their integral structure sheaf: we prove that it is also almost acyclic under log blow-ups in the Kummer \'etale topology. We also supply some foundational results on log adic spaces.
item.dc:creator: Xinyu Shao

item.title: Cohomology of integral structure sheaves for open varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.31289v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the cohomology of integral structure sheaves for two types of open rigid analytic varieties: complements of divisors in quasi-compact varieties, and partially proper spaces. As applications, we prove a strengthened form of the Hebbarkeitssatz (Riemann's extension theorem), involving the almost vanishing of $R^1\lim$, and study pro-\'etale $G$-torsors on open varieties.
item.dc:creator: Xinyu Shao

item.title: Local heights for nef toric compactified divisors
item.description: arXiv:2610.31442v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a definition of a local height of nef toric divisors in the sense of Yuan and Zhang by approximating a height for canonical divisors and then using the local energy to extend to other metrics on the same geometric divisor.
item.dc:creator: Clara Otte

item.title: Deep holes of full-length Reed--Solomon codes: uniform bounds and exact classifications
item.description: arXiv:2610.31460v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $u$ be a received word for the full-length Reed--Solomon code $\operatorname{RS}_q(k)$, with interpolation polynomial $f_u$ of degree $k+m$. For each $m\in\{3,4,5,6,7\}$, we classify all such deep holes over every finite field, without a field-size hypothesis. None occur for odd $m$ in this range. At $m=4$ and $m=6$, the only exceptions are, respectively, the Segre sextic and Frobenius-power families; these occur only in dimension two over fields of characteristic two. For arbitrary $m\geqslant3$, we also establish two uniform bounds. If $\sqrt q\geqslant12(m+1)\log(2m+2)$, no word of interpolation degree $k+m$ is a deep hole when $q$ is odd, $k\geqslant3$, or $m$ is odd. If $q>16(m+2)^4$, we obtain the corresponding complete classification at every admissible $k$, including the explicit dimension-two exceptions. Our proofs use an agreement criterion expressed in complete homogeneous symmetric functions, agreement-count estimates, finite geometry, permutation-polynomial restrictions, and subset constructions for solving the resulting symmetric-function equations. The remaining finite cases are settled by finite computations with supplied certificates and deterministic verification programs.
item.dc:creator: Xiang Fan

item.title: Langlands-Shahidi gamma factors and local transfer in families
item.description: arXiv:2610.31615v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $G$ be a quasi-split $p$-adic group, defined over a non-archimedean local field of residue cardinality $q$, and $R$ be a $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{q}^{-1},\mu_{4p^\infty}]$-algebra. We generalize the constructions of Shahidi local coefficients and Langlands-Shahidi gamma factors to the setting of co-Whittaker $R$-representations. For classical $p$-adic groups, we prove there is a unique integral morphism of endomorphism rings of Gelfand--Graev representations, interpolating the (standard) local generic transfer to a general linear group. This yields a local transfer morphism in families, which allows us to deduce properties of the local $\ell$-adic generic transfer and congruences modulo primes $\ell\neq p$.
item.dc:creator: Johannes Girsch, Robert Kurinczuk

item.title: The Recursive Behavior of the Number of Irreducible Factors of Certain Rational Transformations over Finite Fields
item.description: arXiv:2310.01872v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Constructing irreducible polynomials over finite fields via rational transformations is an active field of study. In this paper, we show that the method can be used for more than that. By considering normalized rational functions $Q$ that generate an invariant subfield $\mathbb{F}_q(x)^G$ of $\mathbb{F}_q(x)$, for a subgroup $G\le Aut(\mathbb{F}_q(x)/\mathbb{F}_q)$, and exploiting the factorization pattern of their rational transformations, we are able to prove that the sets arising from considering whether the rational transformation $f^Q$ has exactly $deg(Q)$ irreducible factors of the same degree as $f$, or an irreducible factor of higher degree, admit a recursive behavior, i.e. their numbers satisfy a recursive equation. These sets occasionally can be described in terms of arithmetical properties the roots of the irreducible polynomials satisfy, e.g. their roots satisfy certain trace or power/non-power conditions. These can often be translated to properties of their minimal polynomials. With that, we prove a new theorem about the number of certain irreducible factors of a class of linearized polynomials, which gives a new context to a recent paper by Granger.
item.dc:creator: Max Schulz

item.title: Relative Trace Formula And Simultaneous Nonvanishing for GL_3 x GL_2 and GL_3 x GL_1 L-functions
item.description: arXiv:2411.12609v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fix a Dirichlet character $\chi$ and a cuspidal GL$(2)$ eigenform $\phi$ with relatively prime conductors. Then we show that there are infinitely many cusp forms $\pi$ on GL$(3)$ such that $L(1/2, \pi \times \chi)$ and $L(1/2, \pi \times \phi)$ are simultaneously non-zero. We achieve this by use of Jacquet's Relative Trace Formula. We derive an expression of the average over the GL$(3)$ cuspidal spectrum as a sum of a non-zero main term and two subsidiary terms which are forced to be zero for large enough level by use of a suitable test function. This modest article is dedicated to the memory of Harish Chandra, on the occasion of his hundredth birthday.
item.dc:creator: Philippe Michel, Dinakar Ramakrishnan, Liyang Yang

item.title: On the Kummer pro-\'etale cohomology of $\mathbb B_{\operatorname{dR}}$
item.description: arXiv:2501.16916v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate $p$-adic cohomologies of log rigid analytic varieties over a $p$-adic field. For a log rigid analytic variety $X$ defined over a discretely valued field, we compute the Kummer pro-\'etale cohomology of $\mathbb{B}_{\mathrm{dR}}^+$ and $\mathbb{B}_{\mathrm{dR}}$. When $X$ is defined over $\mathbb{C}_p$, we introduce a logarithmic ${B}_{\mathrm{dR}}^+$-cohomology theory, serving as a deformation of log de Rham cohomology. Additionally, we establish the log de Rham-\'etale comparison in this setting and prove the degeneration of both the Hodge-Tate and Hodge-log de Rham spectral sequences when $X$ is proper and log smooth.
item.dc:creator: Xinyu Shao

item.title: A partial result towards the Chowla--Milnor conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2505.12687v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Chowla--Milnor conjecture predicts the linear independence of certain Hurwitz zeta values. In this paper, we prove that for any fixed integer $k \geqslant 2$, the dimension of the $\mathbb{Q}$-linear span of $\zeta(k,a/q)-(-1)^{k}\zeta(k,1-a/q)$ ($1 \leqslant a < q/2$, $\gcd(a,q)=1$) is at least $(c -o(1)) \cdot \log q$ as the positive integer $q \to +\infty$ for some absolute constant $c>0$. It is well known that $\zeta(k,a/q)+(-1)^{k}\zeta(k,1-a/q) \in \overline{\mathbb{Q}}\pi^k$, but much less is known previously for $\zeta(k,a/q)-(-1)^{k}\zeta(k,1-a/q)$. Our proof is similar to those of Ball--Rivoal (2001) and Zudilin (2002) concerning the linear independence of Riemann zeta values. However, we use a new type of rational functions to construct linear forms.
item.dc:creator: Li Lai, Jia Li

item.title: Diophantine Equations over $\mathbb Z$: Universal Bounds and Parallel Formalization
item.description:
arXiv:2506.20909v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper explores multiple closely related themes: bounding the complexity of Diophantine equations over the integers and developing mathematical proofs in parallel with formal theorem provers. Hilbert's Tenth Problem (H10) asks about the decidability of Diophantine equations and has been answered negatively by Davis, Putnam, Robinson and Matiyasevich. It is natural to ask for which subclasses of Diophantine equations H10 remains undecidable. Such subclasses can be defined in terms of universal pairs: bounds on the number of variables $
u$ and degree $\delta$ such that all Diophantine equations can be rewritten in at most this complexity. Our work develops explicit universal pairs $(
u, \delta)$ for integer unknowns, focused on reducing the number of unknowns to $
u = 11$. This achieves new bounds that cannot be obtained by naive translations from known results over $\mathbb{N}$. In parallel, we have conducted a formal verification of our results using the proof assistant Isabelle. While formal proof verification has traditionally been applied a posteriori to known results, this project integrates formalization into the discovery and development process. In a final section, we describe key insights gained from this approach and its implications for mathematical practice. Our work contributes both to the study of Diophantine equations and to the broader question of how mathematics is conducted in the 21st century.
item.dc:creator: Jonas Bayer, Marco David, Malte Hassler, Yuri Matiyasevich, Dierk Schleicher

item.title: Regulator Constants and Cohomology
item.description: arXiv:2603.01310v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show how regulator constants of a finitely generated $\mathbb{Z}[G]$-module can be related to $G$-cohomology, where $G$ is a finite group. We then derive consequences of such relation for modules naturally arising in number theory, such as ring of integers and units of number fields, $K$-theory groups of ring of integers and Mordell-Weil groups of elliptic curves.
item.dc:creator: Luca Caputo

item.title: Poly-Bernoulli numbers from shifted log-sine integrals
item.description: arXiv:2603.25392v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 1999, Arakawa and Kaneko introduced a zeta function connecting multiple zeta values with poly-Bernoulli numbers through its special values. Log-sine integrals are also known to be related to zeta values at positive integers. In this article, we study the values of a shifted log-sine integral at negative integers and establish a connection with anti-diagonal sums of poly-Bernoulli numbers. This gives a refinement of Stephan's observation on the central binomial series.
item.dc:creator: Toshiki Matsusaka

item.title: Solutions for Hecke Sum Questions of Banerjee and Bringmann
item.description: arXiv:2605.15107v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We previously conjectured a Hecke-type identity for a series arising from two-color partitions. Banerjee and Bringmann proved the conjecture using modular methods and asked for a direct proof using Bailey pairs. They also suggested investigating the odd part of the series. We answer both questions by applying Bailey's transform to a Bailey pair of Andrews and a conjugate Bailey pair of Lovejoy. Our main theorem gives formulas for the even and odd parts of a series $P_a(q)$ depending on a parameter $a$. The specialization $a=1$ gives the conjectured formula and a companion formula for the odd part.
item.dc:creator: George E. Andrews, Mohamed El Bachraoui

item.title: Homogeneous spaces with transcendental Brauer--Manin obstruction to the Hasse principle
item.description: arXiv:2606.09214v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Over any number field with sufficiently many roots of unity, we construct homogeneous spaces of $\mathbf{SL}_n$ with finite geometric stabilizers of nilpotency class $2$, whose unramified algebraic Brauer group consists only of constant classes, and which has no rational point but has local points in every completion of the ground field. This provides the first known examples of failures of the Hasse principle for homogeneous spaces of connected linear algebraic groups that are detected only by transcendental Brauer classes. The construction builds on the failure of a global--local principle for cup-product decomposition, based on a previous idea of Borovoi and Kunyavskii.
item.dc:creator: Nguyen Manh Linh

item.title: An improvement of the large sieve for square moduli under Hooley's hypothesis $R^*$ for short Sali\'e sums
item.description: arXiv:2609.21195v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $S(Q,M,N,(a_n))=\sum_{q\le Q}\sum_{a\bmod q^2,(a,q)=1}|\sum_{M<n\le M+N}a_ne(an/q^2)|^2$ be Zhao's large sieve sum with square moduli. Zhao conjectured that $S\ll(QN)^\epsilon(Q^3+N)\sum|a_n|^2$. The bound of Baier and Zhao (2008) exceeds this conjecture by a factor which reaches $Q^{1/2}$ at the critical point $N=Q^3$, and there the exponent $1/2$ has not been lowered since. We prove that, under Hooley's Hypothesis $R^*$ for short Sali\'e sums, $S\ll(QN)^\epsilon(Q^3+N+Q^{4/3}N^{2/3})\sum|a_n|^2$. This replaces the excess over Zhao's conjecture by its $2/3$-th power throughout the range $Q^{5/2}<N<Q^4$; at $N=Q^3$ it gives $S\ll Q^{1/2-1/6+\epsilon}N\sum|a_n|^2$. The proof is short. Following Zhao's original treatment, we approximate the point under consideration by fractions $b/r$ with denominators up to $Q^{2/3}N^{1/3}$, which for $N<Q^4$ is beyond the customary $\sqrt{N}$. If the approximation is poor, an elementary count suffices. If it is good, the analytic part of the problem disappears: after Poisson summation in both variables the count is expressed through quadratic Gauss sums, and their exact evaluation at every modulus turns the sum over the dual variable into short Kloosterman and Sali\'e sums, to which Hypothesis $R^*$ applies and gives the square root of the elementary count. At odd moduli the hypothesis is needed only in the form of Conjecture (C*) of Friedlander and Iwaniec. The Gauss-sum evaluations, including even moduli and coefficients sharing a factor with the modulus, are proved in full. This version supersedes earlier versions, which obtained the exponent $1/2-1/28$ at $N=Q^3$ by a much longer route through sums of modular square roots. The paper was prepared in collaboration with Claude (Anthropic).
item.dc:creator: Stephan Baier

item.title: Strongly Pseudoperfect Numbers
item.description: arXiv:2609.36068v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A positive integer $n$ is said to be strongly pseudoperfect if there is a subset $S$ of the positive divisors of $n$ such that $d \in S$ if and only if $n/d \in S$, and $\sum_{d \in S} d = 2n$. We construct new infinite families of strongly pseudoperfect numbers, and also prove new restrictions on when a positive integer $n$ can be strongly pseudoperfect.
item.dc:creator: Audrey Wang, Joshua Zelinsky

item.title: The sixth moment of a degree two $L$-function of arbitrary level
item.description: arXiv:2609.39706v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $f$ be a primitive holomorphic cusp form of arbitrary weight, level and nebentypus. We prove $\int_0^T|L(1/2+it,f)|^6\,dt\ll_{f,\epsilon}T^{2+\epsilon}$, extending Jutila's level-one theorem. The new ingredient is a large sieve comparing the stationary phases in the Booker-Milinovich-Ng transformation at different heights. Applications include moments of order $T^{1+\epsilon}$ on every line to the right of the critical line, $\Omega(T^{4/35-\epsilon})$ simple zeros, zero density estimates, and bounds for cubic-field power sums, shifted convolution sums and the general divisor problem.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Pearce-Crump

item.title: Explicit twists of the Carlitz module and of its tensor powers with unbounded analytic rank
item.description: arXiv:2610.00379v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Grishkov and Logachev have asked (Problem 1.4 of their recent survey) whether, for a fixed finite field F_q, the analytic ranks of the twists of the Carlitz module are bounded. We answer this in the negative for every q >= 3. For q = p^s and n >= 1 put P_{q,n} = (theta^{q^n} - theta)^{q-2}. We show that the directed graph of the matrix M(P_{q,n},1,k) of Grishkov-Logachev has a completely explicit set of circuits: they are pairwise disjoint, none of them meets an entry involving t, and they are in bijection with the orbits of E^n under cyclic rotation, where E = {l in [0,q-2] : p does not divide l+1}. Consequently L(C_{P_{q,n}},t,T) does not depend on t, factors as a product of one term 1 - wt(nu) T^{per(nu)} per orbit, and the analytic rank equals the sum of p^{v_p(per(nu))} over the orbits of weight 1. When n is a power of p this equals (q/p)^n (p-1)^{n-1}, which is unbounded. The argument also answers questions 3.6.1-3.6.4 of the survey for this family. We then compute the L-function for arbitrary nonzero coefficients on supports of the same shape: taking all coefficients equal to -1 multiplies the rank by p-1, and the full support gives twists of degree (q-2)q^n and analytic rank (q-1)^n, the largest rank attainable on such supports. The same method applies to the tensor powers of the Carlitz module: for 1 <= e <= q-2 we obtain twists of the e-th tensor power of analytic rank (q-e)^n, and by a formula of Grishkov and Logachev the same holds for every exponent e = c q^j with 1 <= c <= q-2, with rank (q-c)^n; in particular these analytic ranks are unbounded as well.
item.dc:creator: David Niedbala Giraudin

item.title: Quantitative Gowers uniformity of the primes in intervals of length $X^{5/8+\varepsilon}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.03707v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the first quantitative bounds for the Gowers norms of the von Mangoldt function minus a Siegel corrected model function in short intervals. The result applies to intervals $(X,X+H]$ with $H\geq X^{5/8+\varepsilon}$ and gives quasipolynomial savings for the $U^k(X,X+H]$ norm. The main new ingredient is an efficient non-abelian Type II inverse theorem with explicit dependence on the nilsequence dimension. We prove this inverse theorem by applying Leng's efficient equidistribution theorem directly to an unweighted corner correlation in four variables, hence replacing the factorisation and subgroup argument in the non-abelian Type II proof of Matom\"aki, Shao, Tao and the author. In joint work with Florian Richter, we use this quantitative result as one ingredient in proving the existence of infinitely many sum-product patterns of the form $\{x,x+y,xy\}$ in the shifted primes $\mathbb{P}-1$.
item.dc:creator: Joni Ter\"av\"ainen

item.title: On S\'{a}rk\"{o}zy's Local Extrema Conjectures
item.description: arXiv:2610.08424v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $f: \mathbb{N} \rightarrow (0,\infty)$ be a multiplicative function, and let $\omega > 0$. We consider the frequency with which patterns of the form $$ f(n) > \omega \max\{f(n-1),f(n+1)\}, \quad f(n) < \frac{1}{\omega}\min\{f(n-1),f(n+1)\} $$ occur in the sequence $(f(n))_n$, and give necessary conditions on $f$ so that the set of occurrences of at least one of these patterns has logarithmic density $0$. This includes a complete classification of all such completely multiplicative functions. As a particular application, we characterise (up to prime powers $p^k$, $k \geq 2$) all multiplicative functions $f: \mathbb{N} \rightarrow \mathbb{N}$ that have either finitely many local maxima, or finitely many local minima. This answers, in a strong form, two conjectures of A. S\'{a}rk\"{o}zy from 2001. \\ The proof is based on a natural ``pretentiousness'' dichotomy for additive functions. Key tools in the analysis include an analogue of the Matom\"{a}ki-Radziwi\l\l theorem for additive functions, due to the author, as well as a new bound for the concentration of the gaps $g(n+1)-g(n)$ of an additive function $g$, which may be of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Alexander P. Mangerel

item.title: Discorrelation of the M\"obius function with linear phases in short intervals
item.description: arXiv:2610.11487v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a new approach to studying correlations between arithmetic functions and linear phases with respect to highly irrational frequencies over short intervals. As an application, we prove that \[ \Big|\sum_{x<n \leq x+H}\mu(n) e(n\alpha)\Big| \ll H(\log x)^{-1/3+\varepsilon } \] whenever $x^{0.58+\varepsilon }\leq H\leq x$. In the same range of $H$ we also show that \[ \Big|\sum_{x<n \leq x+H} \Lambda (n) e(n\alpha)\Big| \ll H(\log x)^{-A} \] for arbitrarily large $A>0$ unless there exists an integer $1\leq q\ll (\log x)^{O_A(1)}$ such that $\|q\alpha \| \ll x (\log x)^{O_A(1)}/H^2$. This breaks the $3/5$ barrier in Theorem 1.5 of arXiv:1911.09076v2 and Theorem 2 of [T. Zhan, "On the representation of large odd integer as a sum of three almost equal primes," Acta Mathematica Sinica 7.3 (1991), 259-272]. Moreover, by our method, any improvement in large value estimates for character-twisted Dirichlet polynomials on the critical range would lead to a corresponding improvement in the lower bound for $H$.
item.dc:creator: Javier Pliego, Mengdi Wang

item.title: Imaginary quadratic fields of class number at most 2000
item.description: arXiv:2610.21511v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We determine all imaginary quadratic fields with class number at most 2000, unconditionally: there are 16,453,493 of them, and the largest $|d_K|$ among them is 1,062,350,083. To our knowledge, such a list was previously known only for class number at most 100. We make explicit a recent argument, released by OpenAI and not refereed, that excludes Landau-Siegel zeros: every real zero $\beta$ of $L(s,\chi)$, for a primitive real character $\chi$ of conductor $q\ge3$, satisfies $(1-\beta)\log q\ge5.8\cdot10^{-4}$. An elementary lower bound for $L(1,\chi)$ then shows that a field with class number at most 2000 has $|d_K|<1.61\cdot10^{15}$. The fields with $6\cdot2^{28}\le|d_K|\le1.65\cdot10^{15}$ are excluded by Watkins' sieve, and those below are read from the class group tables of Mosunov and Jacobson. As a consequence, the lists of Cremona and Sutherland of imaginary quadratic orders with class number at most 1000, and the counts of Holmin, Jones, Kurlberg, McLeman and Petersen for odd class numbers up to 1999, previously known under the generalized Riemann hypothesis, hold unconditionally. The two steps, the bound for $\beta$ and the bound for $|d_K|$, are proved in Lean, building on the existing formalization of that argument, and the proofs are checked by two independent kernels. The contributions of AI systems to this work are stated in the paper.
item.dc:creator: Iwao Kimura

item.title: Unconditional Subexponential Arithmetic Circuits for Positive Factorial Multiples
item.description: arXiv:2610.28338v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\tau(n)$ be the least number of binary additions, subtractions and multiplications required to construct $n$ from $1$ and $2$, with reuse of intermediate values. We show that, for every sufficiently large integer $k$, some positive integer $m$ satisfies \[ \tau(mk!)\leq \exp\!\left(O\!\left((\log k)^{2/3}(\log\log k)^{1/3}\right)\right). \] The proof combines unconditional results of Lenstra, Pila and Pomerance on smooth numbers in short intervals and on orders of genus-two Jacobians with a five-parameter family carrying a rational divisor class of infinite order. We encode rational divisor arithmetic, including the tests determining its branches, by a nonzero division-free integer circuit. A common finite sampling space yields circuits whose outputs collectively contain every prime at most $k$, and repeated squaring supplies the required factorial valuations. The circuit bound includes the cost of constructing all integer parameters. This work was carried out with assistance from the UniMath model, developed by UniDT (Shanghai) Co., Ltd., and GPT-6.1 Sol.
item.dc:creator: Liang Zhang

item.title: Ax-Schanuel with derivatives for mixed period mappings
item.description: arXiv:2110.03489v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the Ax-Schanuel property of the derivatives of mixed period mappings. We also prove the jet space reformulation of this result. The proofs use the Ax-Schanuel result for principal bundles with flat connections obtained by Bl\'{a}zquez-Sanz, Casale, Freitag, and Nagloo.
item.dc:creator: Kenneth Chung Tak Chiu

item.title: Formal models for relative adic spaces
item.description: arXiv:2507.11073v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We extend Raynaud's theory of formal models from rigid-analytic spaces over a nonarchimedean field to uniform qcqs adic spaces $X$, with no finite-type assumptions, over an arbitrary Tate affinoid base $S$. The key new ingredient is the notion of a normalized formal blow-up which takes on the role played by admissible formal blow-ups in the classical theory.
item.dc:creator: Dimitri Dine

item.title: On the rational points in conics of a cubic surface
item.description: arXiv:2601.10895v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study rational and integral points lying on finite collections of conics on non-ruled cubic surfaces over a number field. We extend the global determinant method to hypersurfaces in linear subvarieties, retaining dependence on the height of their Cayley forms. The universal Deligne pairing identifies the Chow line bundle on a residual conic pencil with three times of the universal bundle. Uniform bounds for cubic curves then control the number of conics of bounded height and give uniform estimates for their contribution to auxiliary coverings.
item.dc:creator: Chunhui Liu

item.title: On Densities in the Erd\H{o}s-Falconer Distance Problems over the Integers
item.description: arXiv:2610.10665v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Motivated by the classical Erd\H{o}s and Falconer distance problems and Magyar's work on distance sets in $\mathbb Z^d$, we study discrete analogues of the Erd\H{o}s-Falconer unpinned and pinned distance problems over the integers. We ask how the discrete Hausdorff dimension of a set $A\subseteq\mathbb Z^d$ influences the size of its squared-distance sets, measured by generalized upper natural density and upper discrete mass dimension. We propose conjectures for both problems and prove the unpinned conjecture in dimensions $d=1,2,3$ and the pinned conjecture in dimensions $d=1,2$. For the unpinned problem in higher dimensions, we obtain explicit lower bounds for the dimensions of distance sets using elementary integer sphere counting, results on the Erd\H{o}s distinct distances problem, and $\ell^p$-improving inequalities for discrete spherical averages. For the pinned problem, we obtain lower bounds for the dimensions of distance sets for some or every pin. We also establish more general results involving upper discrete mass dimension, upper discrete Banach dimension, and affine dimension, including bounds on the affine dimension of the exceptional set of pins. We construct examples showing that both conjectures are sharp in low dimensions. Further examples demonstrate how the distinctions among discrete Hausdorff dimension, upper discrete mass dimension, and upper discrete Banach dimension lead to different phenomena in the unpinned and pinned distance problems, including limitations on the nontrivial upper bounds these dimensions can provide for the dimensions of distance sets.
item.dc:creator: Eyvindur Ari Palsson, Jian-An Wang
